meta.feature_description: Verify that a logged-in Swag Labs user can add inventory items to the cart from the inventory page, that the per-item button toggles to Remove, the cart-badge counter updates, and the added item appears on the /cart.html page with quantity, name, description, price and a Remove action.
meta.source: https://www.saucedemo.com/ — live UI inspected via Playwright MCP browser tools
assumptions: Application under test is the public Sauce Labs 'Swag Labs' demo site at https://www.saucedemo.com/.
Happy-path user is 'standard_user' with shared password 'secret_sauce' as documented on the login page.
Each scenario assumes a fresh browser session; no state is shared across scenarios.
Product slugs are derived from the product name (e.g. 'Sauce Labs Backpack' -> 'sauce-labs-backpack') and are reflected in the data-test attribute on the Add/Remove button.
Cart badge element is only rendered when count > 0 (absent at zero, present with text content equal to the integer count when > 0).
Prices are displayed in USD with two decimal places prefixed by '$' (e.g. '$29.99').
Inventory sort dropdown defaults to 'Name (A to Z)'; sort order does not affect Add to Cart behavior.

test_cases.title: Logged-in standard_user can add Sauce Labs Backpack to cart from inventory
test_cases.objective: Validate the end-to-end happy path: log in with the documented demo credentials, add a single inventory item, and confirm the per-item button toggles to 'Remove' while the cart badge counter increments to 1.
preconditions: Fresh browser session, no cookies or local storage for saucedemo.com.
Demo account 'standard_user' is in the documented valid users list on the login page and is not in the 'locked_out_user' set.

test_data.notes: Documented valid user on login page
Shared password is 'secret_sauce' as printed on the login page; do not log raw value
First product card in the default A-to-Z sort order; price $29.99

assumptions: Public Sauce Demo environment available, standard_user not temporarily rate-limited

steps.action: Navigate to the Sauce Demo login page
steps.expected_result: Page loads with title 'Swag Labs' and the login form is visible: a Username textbox, a Password textbox, and a Login button. The right-side info panel lists the valid usernames and the shared password.
steps.automation_hint: Wait for the page heading 'Swag Labs' to be visible before proceeding.

steps.action: Enter the standard_user username into the Username textbox
steps.expected_result: The Username field displays 'standard_user' with the text cursor at the end.

steps.action: Enter the shared demo password into the Password textbox
steps.expected_result: The password is masked (each character rendered as a bullet/dot) and the field contains 11 characters.
steps.automation_hint: Reference the element with data-test='password'; assert input type is 'password'.

steps.action: Click the Login button to submit credentials
steps.expected_result: Browser navigates to https://www.saucedemo.com/inventory.html, the 'Products' heading becomes visible, six product cards render in the inventory grid, and the cart badge area in the top-right is empty (no badge number visible).
steps.automation_hint: Reference the button with data-test='login-button'; wait for URL to contain '/inventory.html' and for the 'Products' heading text.

steps.action: Locate the 'Sauce Labs Backpack' product card and confirm its initial Add to cart state
steps.target: Sauce Labs Backpack card on the inventory grid
steps.expected_result: The card displays the product image, name 'Sauce Labs Backpack', description, price '$29.99', and a button labeled 'Add to cart' with classes including 'btn_primary' and data-test 'add-to-cart-sauce-labs-backpack'.
steps.automation_hint: Reference the button with data-test='add-to-cart-sauce-labs-backpack'; assert its accessible text equals 'Add to cart'.

steps.action: Click the 'Add to cart' button on the Sauce Labs Backpack card
steps.target: Add to cart button on Sauce Labs Backpack card
steps.expected_result: Within the same card the button text changes from 'Add to cart' to 'Remove', the button's data-test changes from 'add-to-cart-sauce-labs-backpack' to 'remove-sauce-labs-backpack', the visual class changes from 'btn_primary' to 'btn_secondary', and a cart badge with text '1' appears inside the cart link in the top-right.
steps.automation_hint: After click, wait for the badge element with data-test='shopping-cart-badge' to appear with text '1'.

test_cases.expected_final_state: User remains on the inventory page; the Sauce Labs Backpack card now shows a 'Remove' button; the shopping cart icon in the top-right displays the badge '1'; no other product card state has changed.
expected_post_conditions: Exactly one inventory item (Sauce Labs Backpack) is recorded as added; the cart badge reads '1'.
All other product cards still display 'Add to cart' buttons and have not been mutated.

test_cases.title: Added item appears on /cart.html with quantity 1, full product details, and a working Remove button
test_cases.objective: Verify that after adding a product from the inventory page, navigating to the cart page renders the added item with its quantity, name, description, price and a per-item Remove control, and that the cart badge remains consistent.
preconditions: User is already logged in as 'standard_user' on https://www.saucedemo.com/.
The Sauce Labs Backpack has been added to the cart in this session (cart badge reads '1' on the inventory page).
Browser session is otherwise empty — no other items have been added or removed.

test_data.notes: Added via the inventory Add to cart button
Matches the price displayed on the inventory card

assumptions: User retains their session across the inventory -> cart navigation; cart state is server-session backed by the session cookie.

steps.action: From the inventory page, confirm the cart badge in the top-right reads '1' before navigating
steps.target: Shopping cart link / badge in the header
steps.expected_result: The cart link in the header contains a badge span with text content equal to '1'.
steps.automation_hint: Reference the badge element with data-test='shopping-cart-badge'; assert its text equals '1'.

steps.action: Click the shopping cart icon in the top-right header to open the cart page
steps.target: Shopping cart link in the header
steps.expected_result: Browser navigates to https://www.saucedemo.com/cart.html; the 'Your Cart' page heading is visible; the column headers 'QTY' and 'Description' are shown.
steps.automation_hint: Reference the link with data-test='shopping-cart-link'; wait for URL to contain '/cart.html' and for the 'Your Cart' heading.

steps.action: Locate the cart row for Sauce Labs Backpack and verify the quantity
steps.target: Quantity cell of the Sauce Labs Backpack cart row
steps.expected_result: The quantity cell for the Sauce Labs Backpack row displays the text '1'.
steps.automation_hint: Reference the quantity element with data-test='item-quantity' inside the row whose product name matches 'Sauce Labs Backpack'.

steps.action: Verify the product name, description and price in the Description cell
steps.target: Description cell of the Sauce Labs Backpack cart row
steps.expected_result: The row shows the product name 'Sauce Labs Backpack', the description beginning with 'carry.allTheThings()', and the price '$29.99'.
steps.automation_hint: Reference the elements with data-test='inventory-item-name', 'inventory-item-desc' and 'inventory-item-price' on the matching row.

steps.action: Verify a 'Remove' control is present on the Sauce Labs Backpack row
steps.target: Remove button on the Sauce Labs Backpack cart row
steps.expected_result: A button labeled 'Remove' is present on the row with data-test 'remove-sauce-labs-backpack'.
steps.automation_hint: Reference the button with data-test='remove-sauce-labs-backpack' inside the Sauce Labs Backpack row.

steps.action: Click the 'Remove' button on the Sauce Labs Backpack row
steps.target: Remove button on the Sauce Labs Backpack cart row
steps.expected_result: The Sauce Labs Backpack row is removed from the cart list; the page shows an empty cart state; the cart badge in the header is no longer rendered.
steps.automation_hint: Wait for the row to disappear; assert no element with data-test='inventory-item' remains and no element with data-test='shopping-cart-badge' is present.

test_cases.expected_final_state: The /cart.html page is now empty — the only visible cart-list content is the empty state, the 'Continue Shopping' button and the 'Checkout' button remain. The cart badge in the header is gone.
expected_post_conditions: No items remain in the cart list; the Sauce Labs Backpack row has been removed.
Navigating back to /inventory.html would show the Sauce Labs Backpack card once again displaying 'Add to cart' (per the observed toggle behavior).

open_questions: Should the cart badge ever show a value greater than 1 for a single product (e.g. qty controls)? Observed UI does not expose a quantity stepper on the inventory page; only on the cart page is 'QTY' a static column. Confirm intended behavior if a quantity stepper is later added.
Is there an intended maximum number of items that can be added before the badge text wraps or truncates? Not observed on the live UI today.

Does the cart badge count distinct line items or sum quantities? Observed behavior on this run counted line items (1 line item with quantity 1 produced badge '1'). Confirm whether this holds when a quantity stepper is introduced.
